_about: The vault log of design 2026-11-15-onboarding-trust §3: templates (§3.1), chain (§3.2), state and transitions (§3.3), key commitment (§3.4).
Hand-authored from the independent oracle in tools/vector-gen/oracle (Node WebCrypto and @noble; no andvari code). Regenerate with `npm run generate` there; `npm run check` fails on any difference.
The verifier under test takes the vault id it is checking and the frames from the genesis on, and replays them. It has NO clock: nothing in this file depends on the current time (T2-R-a).

chains: every entry must verify, and the state after entry i must equal entries[i].state. state.head.at is the `at` of the last entry (the value the time rule compares against); members maps userId -> {key, role}; pending and deleted are null for none.

reject: replay the first `after` entries of chain `chain` (all valid), then `frameB64`. The verdict must be expect.verdict, raised at that frame, and the verified state stays the state after entry after-1. A row with its own `vaultId` checks the log as that vault. `signer` names the cast account whose seed signed the frame.

Verdicts in check order (§3.3): bad_frame, unknown_format, non_canonical, bad_statement (the §2 parse); wrong_vault; bad_seq; bad_prev; not_authorized; bad_signature; precondition; fork. Expired-offer clearing runs before not_authorized, and a signer key that does not exist in the state is precondition there (FI-B1).
forks: `seen` is the hash this device already saw at each sequence number. A different entry at a seen position that passes every other check is fork; expect.failedAt is the index of that frame.

checkpoints (§2.4, VR-17): a served chain that verifies (`frames`, from the genesis) compared with a held head `held` = {seq, hash}: a verified head, a device-link checkpoint or the account's vault record. withheld: the chain ends below the held seq. fork: the chain has another hash at the held seq. ok otherwise. It is one pure function of the held head and the served hashes, shared by core and the web twin; instancecard.json's `pinned` rows grade the same function on card chains.

Template rules (VR-1): "a genesis has seq 0 and a zero prev; every other kind has seq >= 1" is checked by the parse (bad_statement). Position is bad_seq and bad_prev alone: a valid genesis placed later is bad_seq, and so is a first entry whose seq is not 0.

vkCommit.derive: hexLower(HKDF-SHA-256(ikm = VK, salt = empty, info = "andvari/v2|vk-commit|" + vaultId, L = 32)). vkCommit.check: whether a candidate key may be used under a state that committed to `vkCommit` (§3.4).

derive.why: the vault key of every chain in this file
the same key under another vault id gives another commitment
another key under the same vault id
31 zero bytes and one 0x01 byte (the lowest key the key floor accepts; an all-zero key is refused as a wiped key)

check.why: another key: refused, nothing is decrypted or written under it
the right key checked against the commitment of another vault id

chains.name: lifecycle
chains.why: Every kind once, with an ownership transfer in the middle: after the accept the new owner signs.

entries.why: the owner adds bob as writer
the owner adds carol as reader
the owner offers the vault to bob for 7 days
a second offer, with the longest lifetime allowed: at + 14 d + 10 min
bob accepts: bob is the owner, alice becomes a writer
the former owner, now a writer, leaves

chains.name: offer-paths
chains.why: Every way a pending offer ends other than accept: cancel by the target, a role change of the target, its removal, its leaving.

entries.why: the target cancels, signing with the key the offer named
a role change of the target clears the offer
removing the target clears the offer
the target leaves: the offer is cleared

chains.name: expiry
chains.why: The time rules: equal `at` values, the shortest offer, an entry at the expiry instant, clearing by a later entry, a new offer over an expired one, accept at the last instant.

entries.why: same `at` as the entry before: allowed, `at` only must not decrease
an entry with at = expiresAt: the offer is not cleared (only at > expiresAt clears)
an entry with at = expiresAt + 1: the expired offer is cleared before the entry is applied
a new offer, to carol, for an hour
an offer while another is pending but expired (pending.expiresAt < at): allowed, it replaces it
accept with at = expiresAt: still in time

chains.name: deleted
chains.why: A deleted vault: the pending offer is cleared, a member can still leave, and the leaver stays out after the restore.

entries.why: delete: deleted = {d1}, and the pending offer is cleared
carol leaves while the vault is deleted (B2)
delete again, with a new deleteId

chains.name: max-at
chains.why: T2-R-a: the shared verifier has no clock. A leave dated 2^53 - 1 is accepted; later entries can only carry that same `at`.

entries.why: bob leaves with at = 2^53 - 1 = 9007199254740991: the verifier ACCEPTS it (the 10-minute ceiling is the server's, 400 at_ahead)
the log is not dead: an entry with the same `at` still verifies

reject.name: add-by-member
reject.why: A non-owner add: bob, a writer, adds dave and signs as himself.

reject.name: add-owner-named-member-signed
reject.why: The statement names the owner as actor, but bob's key signed it.

reject.name: add-owner-signed-member-named
reject.why: The owner's key signed, but the actor is bob: the actor must be the owner.

reject.name: add-by-outsider
reject.why: eve, who is not in the vault, adds herself.

reject.name: add-existing-member
reject.why: The owner adds bob, who is already a member.

reject.name: add-the-owner
reject.why: The owner adds herself: the owner is in members.

reject.name: add-after-delete
reject.why: add after delete: the vault is deleted.

reject.name: role-by-member
reject.why: bob, a writer, changes carol's role.

reject.name: role-of-non-member
reject.why: A role change for dave, who is not a member.

reject.name: role-of-owner
reject.why: A role change for the owner.

reject.name: role-after-delete
reject.why: A role change while the vault is deleted.

reject.name: remove-by-member
reject.why: bob, a writer, removes carol.

reject.name: remove-non-member
reject.why: Removing dave, who is not a member.

reject.name: remove-the-owner
reject.why: The owner removes herself.

reject.name: remove-after-delete
reject.why: A remove while the vault is deleted.

reject.name: leave-by-owner
reject.why: leave by the owner: the signer key exists (it is the owner key), the row condition actor != owner fails.

reject.name: leave-by-non-member
reject.why: FI-B1: leave by dave, who is not in members. The key the row names, members[actor].key, does not exist.

reject.name: leave-by-non-member-bad-signature
reject.why: FI-B1: checking stops at the undefined key, so the same leave with a broken signature is still precondition, not bad_signature.
reject.signer: dave, then one signature bit flipped

reject.name: leave-signed-by-another-member
reject.why: A leave naming carol, signed by bob: the signer must map to members[carol].key.

reject.name: leave-twice
reject.why: bob left in the last entry; a second leave finds him outside members.

reject.name: offer-by-member
reject.why: bob, a writer, offers the vault to carol.

reject.name: offer-to-non-member
reject.why: An offer to dave, who is not a member.

reject.name: offer-to-owner
reject.why: An offer to the owner herself.

reject.name: offer-wrong-tokey
reject.why: An offer to bob with a wrong toKey (carol's key): toKey must equal members[to].key.

reject.name: offer-while-pending
reject.why: An offer while another is pending and not expired.

reject.name: offer-too-long
reject.why: An offer one millisecond too long: expiresAt = at + 14 d + 10 min + 1.

reject.name: offer-expires-at-at
reject.why: An offer with expiresAt = at: the row needs at < expiresAt.

reject.name: offer-expires-before-at
reject.why: An offer that expired before it was signed.

reject.name: offer-after-delete
reject.why: An offer while the vault is deleted.

reject.name: offer-at-max-ms
reject.why: T2-R-a: after the leave dated 2^53 - 1, an offer must carry at = 2^53 - 1, and no expiresAt can be later: at = expiresAt = 2^53 - 1 fails at < expiresAt. Ownership of this vault is frozen, which is why the SERVER refuses a far-future `at`; the verifier itself stays clock-free.

reject.name: cancel-by-third-party
reject.why: cancel by a third party: carol is neither the owner nor the offer's target.

reject.name: cancel-target-named-other-key
reject.why: A cancel naming the target (bob) but signed by carol.

reject.name: cancel-owner-named-target-signed
reject.why: A cancel naming the owner as actor but signed with the target's key: for the owner the signer must be the owner key.

reject.name: cancel-wrong-offer-id-owner
reject.why: The owner cancels an offerId that is not the pending one.

reject.name: cancel-wrong-offer-id-target
reject.why: The target cancels an offerId that is not the pending one.

reject.name: cancel-no-pending-owner
reject.why: The owner cancels when nothing is pending: the key exists, the row condition pending != none fails.

reject.name: cancel-no-pending-target
reject.why: FI-B1: a cancel by the (former) target with no pending offer; o1 was cancelled by the owner in the entry before. The key the row names, pending.toKey, does not exist.

reject.name: cancel-after-expiry-owner
reject.why: The owner cancels with at = expiresAt + 1: the expired offer is cleared before the entry is checked, so nothing is pending.

reject.name: accept-by-non-target
reject.why: accept by a non-target: carol accepts the offer made to bob.

reject.name: accept-target-named-owner-signed
reject.why: An accept naming the target but signed by the owner's key.

reject.name: accept-by-owner
reject.why: The owner accepts her own offer: the actor must be pending.to.

reject.name: accept-wrong-offer-id
reject.why: The target accepts with the wrong offerId.

reject.name: accept-after-expiry
reject.why: accept after expiry (at = expiresAt + 1): the clearing runs before step 5, so pending is none and the key the row names does not exist (FI-B1).

reject.name: accept-no-pending
reject.why: FI-B1: accept with no pending offer.

reject.name: accept-cancelled-offer
reject.why: Accepting an offer the owner cancelled.

reject.name: accept-after-owner-signed-past-expiry
reject.why: T-R1: the owner signed an entry dated after the expiry, which cleared the offer; a late accept is impossible whatever `at` it carries.

reject.name: accept-after-delete
reject.why: The delete cleared the pending offer.

reject.name: delete-by-member
reject.why: bob, a writer, deletes the vault.

reject.name: delete-while-deleted
reject.why: A second delete while the vault is deleted.

reject.name: restore-wrong-delete-id
reject.why: restore with the wrong deleteId.

reject.name: restore-not-deleted
reject.why: A restore of a vault that is not deleted.

reject.name: restore-by-member
reject.why: bob, a writer, restores the vault.

reject.name: at-decreases
reject.why: T-R1: `at` one millisecond below the previous entry's.

reject.name: seq-skips
reject.why: seq = head.seq + 2.

reject.name: seq-repeats
reject.why: seq = head.seq, with prev still naming the head.

reject.name: prev-names-older-entry
reject.why: prev is the hash of the entry before the head.

reject.name: prev-zero
reject.why: prev is 64 zeros on a later entry.

reject.name: wrong-vault
reject.why: An entry the owner really signed, at the right position, for another vault id.

reject.name: wrong-vault-genesis
reject.why: The genesis of vault aaaa… served as the log of vault bbbb…: the verifier is told which vault it is checking.

reject.name: genesis-seq-not-zero
reject.why: A genesis the creator signed with seq 1. "A genesis has seq 0" is a template rule, so the parse refuses it before any position check.

reject.name: genesis-prev-not-zero
reject.why: A genesis whose prev is not 64 zeros.

reject.name: first-entry-add-with-seq-0
reject.why: A first entry that is an add with seq 0: every kind but genesis has seq >= 1.

reject.name: later-entry-with-seq-0
reject.why: An add with seq 0 after three entries: the template rule fails at the parse, before bad_seq.

reject.name: genesis-with-a-later-seq
reject.why: A genesis whose seq and prev fit position 3: still bad_statement, a genesis has seq 0.

reject.name: first-entry-add-with-seq-1
reject.why: A first entry that is a well-formed add with seq 1: position is bad_seq.

reject.name: genesis-placed-later
reject.why: The chain's own valid genesis frame served again at position 3: bad_seq.

reject.name: another-genesis-placed-later
reject.why: Another valid genesis for the same vault at position 3: bad_seq.

reject.name: order-vault-before-seq
reject.why: Wrong vault and wrong seq: wrong_vault comes first.

reject.name: order-seq-before-prev
reject.why: Wrong seq and wrong prev: bad_seq comes first.

reject.name: order-prev-before-authorization
reject.why: Wrong prev, signed by a non-owner: bad_prev comes first.

reject.name: order-authorization-before-signature
reject.why: A non-owner add whose signature is also broken: not_authorized comes first.
reject.signer: bob, then one signature bit flipped

reject.name: order-signature-before-precondition
reject.why: The owner adds an existing member and the signature is broken: bad_signature comes first.
reject.signer: alice, then one signature bit flipped

reject.name: order-parse-before-vault
reject.why: A statement with a space after a colon, for another vault: the parse comes first.

reject.name: other-purpose-frame
reject.why: A well-formed instance-card frame (purpose 0x04) where a log entry is expected.

reject.name: truncated-frame
reject.why: The next entry cut off inside its signature.

reject.name: unknown-format
reject.why: The next entry with format byte 0x03 in the magic.

reject.name: unknown-kind
reject.why: kind "rename" is not one of the ten kinds: the value fails its type, and no template exists to re-encode it.

reject.name: role-owner-in-add
reject.why: An add with "role":"owner": the role type is writer or reader.

reject.name: add-without-grant-id
reject.why: An add with no grantId: every key of the kind's template is required.

reject.name: leave-with-extra-field
reject.why: A leave carrying a member field: leave has no extra fields.

reject.name: version-3
reject.why: A canonical entry with "v":3.

reject.name: purpose-literal-mismatch
reject.why: Purpose code 0x03 with the literal "instance-card" and an add's key set.

reject.name: signature-flipped
reject.why: A valid add by the owner with one signature bit flipped.
reject.signer: alice, then one signature bit flipped

reject.name: statement-changed-after-signing
reject.why: The owner signed role reader; the statement in the frame says writer (still canonical).

reject.name: signer-negated-point
reject.why: signerPub replaced by -A, the owner key with the sign bit of x flipped, under the signature the owner made as A. A and -A have the same X25519 image, so the signer binding passes, and this frame then fails the signature check only because nobody signed again. That check stops a third party, who cannot sign for -A; it does not stop the key's holder, who can sign validly under A or under -A. The vault log binds its signer through the image and so does not tell the two apart; where they must be told apart, what refuses -A is a byte comparison of the signer key (the card chain and the operator's own key in instancecard.json, §4.1; the extension's genesis check in accountgenesis.json).

reject.name: signer-identity-point
reject.why: signerPub is the Edwards identity point (small order): it has no X25519 image, so it maps to nobody's key.

reject.name: signer-all-zero
reject.why: signerPub is 32 zero bytes (a point of order 4).
reject.signer: alice; signerPub then replaced by 32 zero bytes

reject.name: genesis-signer-not-owner-key
reject.why: A genesis whose ownerKey is alice's but which bob signed: the creator must sign with the key the genesis names.

reject.name: genesis-signature-flipped
reject.why: The genesis with one signature bit flipped.
reject.signer: alice, then one signature bit flipped

forks.name: same-entries-again
forks.why: The device saw entries 0..2 and is served the same three frames: no fork.

forks.name: different-entry-at-seen-seq
forks.why: Two entries at one position: the device saw "add carol as reader" at seq 2 and is served a different, validly signed "add carol as writer" at seq 2.

forks.name: fork-stops-the-replay
forks.why: The other branch continues with a valid entry at seq 3; the verdict is fork at seq 2 and nothing after it is applied.

forks.name: different-invalid-entry-is-not-a-fork
forks.why: A different entry at a seen position that does not verify is its own verdict: a fork needs two VALID entries.

forks.name: different-genesis
forks.why: Another validly signed genesis for the same vault id.

forks.name: beyond-what-was-seen
forks.why: The device saw entries 0..2; entries 3 and 4 are new and extend the same chain.

checkpoints.name: head-is-the-checkpoint
checkpoints.why: The served chain ends at the held head.

checkpoints.name: chain-extends-the-checkpoint
checkpoints.why: The served chain holds the held hash at its seq and goes on.

checkpoints.name: withheld-chain-ends-below
checkpoints.why: Withholding: the served chain ends at seq 2, below the held head at seq 4. The device keeps its own state.

checkpoints.name: withheld-one-short
checkpoints.why: The served chain ends one entry below the held head.

checkpoints.name: withheld-nothing-served
checkpoints.why: No entry is served at all.

checkpoints.name: fork-another-entry-at-the-checkpoint
checkpoints.why: The served chain has a different, validly signed entry at the held seq.

checkpoints.name: fork-on-a-longer-chain
checkpoints.why: The other branch goes on past the held seq: still a fork.

checkpoints.name: fork-another-genesis
checkpoints.why: A held head at seq 0 against another validly signed genesis.
